problem_type: Priced paid-card parameter chips hidden, overlapped, or scrolled away by a width-measurement layout policy
symptom: In the Agent panel paid card, a Seedance 2.0 card at the production 390px width drew 16:9 on top of the variant chip (标准 / Standard); at 300px English the variant chip left the card and all three priced chips (aspect ratio, duration, resolution) moved into the gear panel. The previous follow-up kept the chips but made the row horizontally scrollable.
direct_cause: useFittedChipCount decided how many primary chips to show from scrollWidth versus clientWidth. The identity row (model + variant) was one min-w-0 flex item, so it shrank and its shrink-0 children spilled over the next chip without making the row report overflow; when overflow was detected, planParameterChips demoted priced chips from the tail into the gear panel. 712ff9ba7 then ignored the measured count and added overflow-x-auto, which keeps the chips in the DOM but out of sight.
class_root: Visibility of priced/output controls on the spend confirmation surface depended on a runtime width measurement. Any measurement blind spot (shrinking wrappers, fonts, first-frame width, viewport) could hide a value the user is about to pay for, and the only alternatives offered were demotion or scrolling, both of which hide it.
affected_population: Every chips-layout InlineParameterBar: the Agent panel paid confirmation card (NodeGenerationComposer host=panel) and the design-lab chips demo (both deleted 2026-10-24)
Models whose primary chips plus identity chips exceed the card width: Seedance 2.0 with its variant axis at 390px, any model in English or with a narrow panel
entry_points: InlineParameterBar renders one summary pill and one body-portal panel for every host (canvas node, storyboard row, storyboard bulk bar, design lab); the paid card is no longer a host (2026-10-24: it shows node pointers and a read-only summary).
internal_only_reason: Which parameters must stay visible before a paid generation is Nomi's spend-card domain rule; CSS flex-wrap is the platform layout primitive used to satisfy it and needs no library decision.
invariants: The paid card carries no parameter controls: priced and output values are changed on the node, so no width measurement on the spend surface can demote or hide a control.
The node composer's parameter bar renders one summary pill and one panel portalled to the body; it reads no layout measurement, and the panel is never clipped by the React Flow node.
The card's one-line summary is read-only and never offers a control; when prices differ the per-shot fold lists every shot's values.

door_reduction.why_not: The four call sites are four hosts of the one component (canvas node, storyboard row, storyboard bulk bar, design lab) plus its definition; the paid card is not one of them any more, and splitPrimaryParameterControls with its two doors is deleted.

generality_proof: There is one placement left (summary pill + body portal panel) shared by every host, and the paid card renders no parameter component at all (depcruise chat-card-no-import-node-editor keeps chat cards from importing the composer or its controls), so no caller, font, platform or viewport can bring a measured layout back without re-adding a layout that the tests reject.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Renders the node composer's parameters as one summary pill and one body-portal panel; no chips layout and no layout measurement remain.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The only layout left; InlineParameterBar.test.ts pins the pill and the portal panel, param-panel-numeric.e2e.mjs checks the panel is outside the React Flow node.
Renders NodePointer / NodePointerGroup and a read-only summary line; it imports no parameter control (design-lab-spend-card.walk.mjs asserts no editor inside the card).

recurrence.reason: New models with variant axes, longer English labels and narrower panels push any row past one line; a measurement-based policy would again hide a priced value somewhere, so the paid card carries no controls and the composer keeps one unmeasured placement.
same_class_scan: node scripts/door-map.mjs --write=InlineParameterBar (2026-10-24: 4 hosts; the paid card is not one)
git grep parameterLayout src -> none (the chips layout is deleted)

prevention.invariant: Parameters render in one placement (summary pill + body portal panel) with no measurement input; the paid card renders none.
prevention.failure_mode: A narrow card truncates its one read-only summary line with an ellipsis (the title attribute shows the whole line); the values are complete on the node.
prevention.strategy: Delete the chips / stacked / inline-panel layouts together with the panel host; the card points at the node instead of embedding its composer.

legacy_paths.rationale: 2026-10-24, deleted in place: InlineParameterBar's chips / stacked / inline-panel layouts, splitPrimaryParameterControls and the chip helpers in primaryParameterChips, and NodeGenerationComposer's panel host. No fallback layout remains.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Layout uses the browser's flex-wrap; no third-party runtime decides the invariant.

migration: No persisted state changes; the paid card simply grows a row when the chips do not fit. 2026-10-24 D2 step 3 (design card docs/plan/2026-10-23-d2-pointer-spend-card.md; contract docs/fixes/2026-10-24-spend-card-one-engine.root-cause.json): the paid card became node pointers plus a read-only summary that hands its shots to the canvas engine; the chips layout (InlineParameterBar chips + splitPrimaryParameterControls, mounted by the panel host) was deleted with the old card, so this contract's boundaries, doors, tests and legacy paths were re-pointed to the code that holds the invariant today (problem, symptom, causes and class root above are the original record).
residual_risks: The paid card's summary line truncates at narrow widths (ellipsis plus a title tooltip), as on the approved SpendCardQ1 board; the full values are on the node, and in the per-shot fold when prices differ.
